label: Confirmed Deaths
source: Government/Defensoría del Pueblo tallies (as of Jul 9, 2026)
contestNote: Union and independent sources dispute how many deaths are directly attributable to blockade-caused hospital shortages (~14 of the total) versus other causes.

label: State of Emergency
source: Government of Bolivia / Interior Minister Marco Oviedo, Sep 13, 2026
deltaNote: The original 90-day decree expires Sep 18, 2026. After the Chamber of Deputies' Plural Justice Commission unanimously approved a resolution Sep 10 to extend it 90 more days, Interior Minister Marco Oviedo announced Sep 13 the executive will formally send the Legislative Assembly a decree for the extension, citing "gran consenso ciudadano." Opposition mounted quickly Sep 14: the Senate's Libre bloc said it would oppose the measure and the National Congress of Free Transport rejected it, arguing a state of exception "should not be used to limit social protest"; a floor vote in the Chamber and a joint session with the Senate are expected the following week. Evo Morales called the measure already ineffective Sep 12, accusing Defense Minister Justiniano of negotiating directly with Beni blockaders rather than enforcing it, and warned an extension would be "worse."

label: Active Blockades
source: La Razón / FM La Paz, Sep 11, 2026
deltaNote: San Pablo bridge (Marbán province, Beni) blockade was lifted Aug 30 after a 4-day standoff, with the government pledging Bs. 9.80/L diesel capped at 120L weekly for the province. Seven Santa Cruz moto-taxi federations set an indefinite blockade at 13+ points for Sep 11 over fuel shortages and price increases, then called it off after overnight talks with Hydrocarbons Minister Marcelo Blanco and YPFB — organizers call it a 'recess,' not a resolution, and set Oct 10 as their checkpoint. Yapacaní's status as of Sept 3 was unconfirmed since; Decree 5676's Bs. 18/liter large-consumer tier remains unrepealed. Evo Morales said Sep 12 the lack of security-force enforcement at San Pablo shows the state of exception is no longer being applied.

label: USD Exchange Rate (floated)
source: Central Bank of Bolivia (official TCO, Sep 12, 2026)
deltaNote: Rate climbed further from Sep 4's Bs. 12.45 to a new record Bs. 12.64 around Sep 9-10, then eased for three straight sessions — Bs. 12.42 (Sep 10), Bs. 12.04 (Sep 11), Bs. 11.53 (Sep 12) — after the BCB suspended new dollar-purchase operations (Sep 7), created a Restricted Monetary Reserve under Resolution RD Nº 131/2026 (Sep 8), and began direct dollar distribution to private financial-system entities (Sep 9) to curb what it called 'unnecessary shocks' in the currency market. Still up sharply from the 15-year peg of Bs. 6.96 before the Jun 29 float.

label: Inflation (y/y)
contestNote: The IMF forecasts full-year 2026 inflation near 20.7%, but Bolivia's statistics institute (INE) reported an official year-on-year print of just 4.93% for July 2026 — pass-through from the June currency float and December fuel-subsidy cuts had not yet fully hit consumer prices.

label: Diesel Price — Large Consumers (GRACOS)
deltaNote: Up from the prior Bs. 9.80-9.90/L rate; the subsidized Bs. 9.80/L price is unchanged for transport operators and individual consumers
contestNote: Facing backlash over the 84% hike, Deputy Hydrocarbons Minister Hernán Paredes said Aug 25 the decree "has to be modified" toward a more competitive price. But Minister of the Presidency Fernando Aramayo rejected repeal on Aug 27, attributing the decree to IMF conditionality; new blockades against it began Aug 26 in Beni and Oruro. New Economy Minister Christian Morales Burgos, sworn in Aug 25 replacing interim minister Óscar Mario Justiniano, said Aug 26 the decree needs adjustments "to minimize risks" from producer mobilizations; the Pro Santa Cruz Civic Committee set a 72-hour ultimatum (deadline Sun Aug 30) to repeal it before escalating to a region-wide Asamblea de la Cruceñidad.

label: Arrests (crisis-related)
contestNote: MAS-aligned and union groups characterize a portion of arrests and the Evo Morales warrant as politically motivated prosecution.

label: Cerimedo-Linked Detentions
value: 4 held + 1 arrest ordered; Cerimedo faces 3 investigations
deltaNote: Protected witness Nadia Beller testified Aug 30 alleging Cerimedo and First Lady Urquidi ran a scheme diverting ~2 million liters/day of fuel from YPFB (~Bs. 1M/day on the black market), linking Cerimedo to a Jul 23 attempt to fly 189kg of gold (~$25M) out of Viru Viru airport to Dubai, and to suspected drug trafficking via Beni airstrips — none of these specific allegations have resulted in charges yet. Separately, VP Lara announced Sep 8 he will formally propose President Paz as a witness in the case and challenged him to a face-to-face confrontation, saying he personally saw Cerimedo giving orders to ministers in two cabinet meetings; Paz has not accepted. Santa Cruz prosecutors ordered the Aug 31 arrest of María Argentina Rojas Roca, a former Viru Viru Customs chief, as an alleged coordinator/paymaster of the gunmen who shot Beller; Cerimedo remains under two preventive detention orders (attempted femicide at Palmasola, illicit enrichment at Chonchocoro).

label: YPFB State Intervention
source: Government of Bolivia, Supreme Decree 5697, Sep 2, 2026
deltaNote: President Paz placed state oil company YPFB under "extraordinary, transparent and temporary" intervention for up to 180 days (extendable once by 90), via a commission of the Economy, Production/Environment/Water, Hydrocarbons/Energy and Public Works ministries, to audit the fuel import/distribution chain and trace smuggling and diversion networks. The decree does not dissolve YPFB or change its legal status.
